command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
: > perc1.log; : > perc2.log; : > perc3.log

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# This is a single-tool bioconda image around a C++ binary, so it may ship no interpreter --
# every check below is awk, which is why none of them reach for python3.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
# pins.sha256 covers every input the RECIPE stages; this task stages a subset of them, so
# --ignore-missing is required -- plain `sha256sum -c` fails on a file it was never given.
# That flag alone would pass vacuously if nothing were staged, so the number actually verified
# is asserted too.
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: a staged file does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
NOK=$(sha256sum -c --ignore-missing pins.sha256 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': OK$')
printf 'pinned_files_verified\t%s\n' "$NOK"
test "$NOK" -eq 1 || { echo "FAIL: verified $NOK pinned files, expected 1"; exit 1; }
PROW=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="pin_psm_rows"{print $2}' expected.tsv)
PTGT=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="pin_targets"{print $2}'  expected.tsv)
PDEC=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="pin_decoys"{print $2}'   expected.tsv)
printf 'pin_psm_rows\t%s\npin_targets\t%s\npin_decoys\t%s\n' "$PROW" "$PTGT" "$PDEC"

command -v percolator >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL: percolator absent from this image"; exit 1; }
# Do not redirect stderr here: percolator prints its banner to stderr, and a `command not
# found` swallowed by 2>/dev/null surfaces later as an empty version and a message that
# blames the fixture.
PV=$(percolator -h 2>&1 | grep -oiE 'percolator version [0-9a-z.,-]+' | head -1)
echo "percolator_version	${PV:-unknown}"

run_perc () {  # $1 = seed, $2 = tag
  percolator -U -S "$1" \
    -m "t_$2.tab" -M "d_$2.tab" \
    percolatorTab > "perc_$2.stdout" 2> "perc_$2.log"
  local rc=$?
  printf 'percolator_rc_seed%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$rc"
  if [ "$rc" != "0" ]; then tail -15 "perc_$2.log"; return 1; fi
  test -s "t_$2.tab" || { echo "FAIL: seed $1 produced no target results"; return 1; }
  return 0
}

echo "== run percolator three times: the same seed twice, then a different one =="
T0=$(date +%s)
run_perc 1 a || { echo "FAIL: percolator failed (seed 1, run a)"; exit 1; }
run_perc 1 b || { echo "FAIL: percolator failed (seed 1, run b)"; exit 1; }
run_perc 7 c || { echo "FAIL: percolator failed (seed 7)"; exit 1; }
T1=$(date +%s)
printf 'percolator_wall_s_3runs\t%s\n' "$((T1-T0))"
cp perc_a.log perc1.log; cp perc_b.log perc2.log; cp perc_c.log perc3.log

echo "== the output's shape, read from its header rather than assumed =="
head -1 t_a.tab | tr '\t' '\n' | nl | sed 's/^/  /'
# Resolve the columns by NAME. Percolator writes PSMId/score/q-value/posterior_error_prob/
# peptide/proteinIds, and a positional guess breaks silently if that order ever changes.
COLS=$(awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) printf "%s=%d ", $i, i; exit}' t_a.tab)
echo "resolved_columns	$COLS"
IDX=$(awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){if($i=="PSMId")a=i; if($i=="score")b=i;
      if($i=="q-value")c=i; if($i=="posterior_error_prob")d=i}
      if(!a||!b||!c||!d){print "0 0 0 0"; exit} print a" "b" "c" "d; exit}' t_a.tab)
read -r CID CSC CQ CPEP <<< "$IDX"
printf 'col_PSMId\t%s\ncol_score\t%s\ncol_qvalue\t%s\ncol_PEP\t%s\n' "$CID" "$CSC" "$CQ" "$CPEP"
test "$CID" != "0" || { echo "FAIL: could not resolve PSMId/score/q-value/PEP by name"; exit 1; }

# -------------------------------------------- IDENTITY 1: every input PSM comes back out, once
NT=$(awk 'NR>1' t_a.tab | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
ND=$(awk 'NR>1' d_a.tab | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
printf 'out_target_rows\t%s\nout_decoy_rows\t%s\nout_total_rows\t%s\n' "$NT" "$ND" "$((NT+ND))"
test "$((NT+ND))" -eq "$PROW" || {
  echo "FAIL: $((NT+ND)) rows out of $PROW in -- rescoring dropped or duplicated PSMs"; exit 1; }
test "$NT" -eq "$PTGT" || { echo "FAIL: $NT target rows, PIN declares $PTGT"; exit 1; }
test "$ND" -eq "$PDEC" || { echo "FAIL: $ND decoy rows, PIN declares $PDEC"; exit 1; }
echo "identity_conservation	every one of $PROW input PSMs appears exactly once, in the right file"

# ------------- IDENTITY 2: every row sits in the file its own protein names say it should
# The obvious version of this check -- join each output row back to the PIN's Label column by
# SpecId -- DOES NOT WORK, and not because percolator is wrong: SpecId is not unique in a PIN.
# `103111-Yeast-2hr-01_27_3_1` appears twice, so a SpecId->Label map silently keeps whichever
# row came last and the comparison then reports thousands of false misplacements.
#
# So the check uses the convention carried by each row ITSELF: a decoy PSM's proteins all start
# with decoy_, a target PSM's never do. That is anchored to the Label column at staging time,
# where all 19,674 PIN rows were verified to agree. Note proteinIds is itself TAB-SEPARATED and
# spills across columns 6..NF, so every protein field is examined, not just the last one.
BAD=$(awk -F'\t' '
  FNR == 1 { next }
  {
    ndec = 0; ntot = 0
    for (i = 6; i <= NF; i++) {
      if ($i == "") continue
      ntot++
      if ($i ~ /^decoy_/) ndec++
    }
    if (ntot == 0) { noprot++; next }
    isdec = (ndec == ntot)
    ismix = (ndec > 0 && ndec < ntot)
    want  = (FILENAME ~ /^d_/)
    if (ismix) mixed++
    else if (isdec != want) wrong++
  }
  END { printf "%d %d %d", wrong + 0, mixed + 0, noprot + 0 }' t_a.tab d_a.tab)
read -r MISPLACED MIXED NOPROT <<< "$BAD"
printf 'rows_in_the_wrong_class\t%s\nrows_mixing_target_and_decoy_proteins\t%s\nrows_with_no_protein\t%s\n' \
  "$MISPLACED" "$MIXED" "$NOPROT"
test "$NOPROT"   -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: $NOPROT output rows carry no protein at all"; exit 1; }
test "$MISPLACED" -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: $MISPLACED PSMs landed in the wrong class file"; exit 1; }
echo "identity_partition	every PSM is in the file its own protein names require ($MIXED mixed)"

# ------------------------------ IDENTITY 3: q-value is monotone non-decreasing as score falls
# A q-value is the minimum FDR at which a PSM is accepted, so walking down the score ranking it
# can never decrease. Exact ordering property -- no tolerance on any value.
#
# WITH ONE REFINEMENT THAT IS NOT A FUDGE. percolator prints score to 6 significant figures, so
# two PSMs whose true scores differ slightly print the SAME score while carrying legitimately
# different q-values. Counting those as violations measures the output's print precision, not
# the tool -- it reported 2 on targets and 82 on decoys, every one at a tied printed score. So
# ties may fall in any internal order (q sorted ascending within a score) and the ordering is
# asserted ACROSS score groups, which is the actual claim. Tied groups are reported, not hidden.
for f in t_a.tab d_a.tab; do
  V=$(awk -F'\t' -v CSC="$CSC" -v CQ="$CQ" 'NR>1 {print $CSC"\t"$CQ}' "$f" \
      | sort -k1,1gr -k2,2g \
      | awk -F'\t' '{ if (NR>1 && $2 < prev - 1e-12) n++; prev=$2 } END{print n+0}')
  TIE=$(awk -F'\t' -v CSC="$CSC" -v CQ="$CQ" 'NR>1 {
          if ($CSC in lo) { if ($CQ<lo[$CSC]) lo[$CSC]=$CQ; if ($CQ>hi[$CSC]) hi[$CSC]=$CQ }
          else { lo[$CSC]=$CQ; hi[$CSC]=$CQ } }
        END { for (k in lo) if (hi[k] > lo[k]) n++; print n+0 }' "$f")
  printf 'q_monotonicity_violations_%s\t%s\n' "$f" "$V"
  printf 'tied_printed_scores_with_differing_q_%s\t%s\n' "$f" "$TIE"
  test "$V" -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: q-values decrease across score groups in $f"; exit 1; }
done
RANGE=$(awk -F'\t' -v CQ="$CQ" -v CPEP="$CPEP" 'NR>1 {
    if ($CQ<0||$CQ>1) q++; if ($CPEP<0||$CPEP>1) p++ } END{printf "%d %d", q+0, p+0}' t_a.tab)
read -r QOUT POUT <<< "$RANGE"
printf 'qvalues_outside_0_1\t%s\nPEPs_outside_0_1\t%s\n' "$QOUT" "$POUT"
test "$QOUT" -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: $QOUT q-values outside [0,1]"; exit 1; }
test "$POUT" -eq 0 || { echo "FAIL: $POUT posterior error probabilities outside [0,1]"; exit 1; }
echo "identity_qvalue	q-values and PEPs lie in [0,1] and q is monotone in score"

# ---------------- CONSISTENCY: the decoy fraction tracks the q threshold it was accepted at
# This is a BOUND, not an identity, and the distinction matters. percolator's q comes from its
# own target-decoy estimator after SVM rescoring; the raw decoy fraction among accepted PSMs is
# a DIFFERENT estimator of the same quantity, so demanding they match would be comparing two
# methods and calling the gap an error. What must hold is agreement in MAGNITUDE -- FDR control
# that was actually broken would be off by an order of magnitude, not a few percent.
for T in 0.01 0.05; do
  R=$(awk -F'\t' -v CQ="$CQ" -v T="$T" 'FNR==1{next} $CQ<=T { n++; if (FILENAME ~ /^d_/) d++ }
       END { if (n+0==0) print "0 0 NA"; else printf "%d %d %.4f", n, d+0, (d+0)/n }' t_a.tab d_a.tab)
  read -r NACC NDEC FRAC <<< "$R"
  printf 'accepted_at_q%s\t%s\ndecoys_among_accepted_q%s\t%s\ndecoy_fraction_q%s\t%s\n' \
    "$T" "$NACC" "$T" "$NDEC" "$T" "$FRAC"
  test "$NACC" -gt 0 || { echo "FAIL: nothing accepted at q<=$T -- the check would be vacuous"; exit 1; }
  awk -v f="$FRAC" -v t="$T" 'BEGIN { printf "fraction_over_threshold_q%s\t%.2fx\n", t, f/t }'
  awk -v f="$FRAC" -v t="$T" 'BEGIN { exit !(f <= 2 * t) }' || {
    echo "FAIL: decoy fraction $FRAC at q<=$T is more than twice the threshold"; exit 1; }
done
echo "identity_fdr	the decoy fraction among accepted PSMs is bounded by its own q threshold"

# ------------------- IDENTITY 5: the SVM is seeded, so the same seed must be bit-reproducible
# Percolator trains a support-vector machine on randomised cross-validation splits, so the
# ranking it returns is a property of the seed as well as the data. An exact assertion on any
# of the numbers above is only meaningful once that is pinned, which is what this checks.
HA=$(sha256sum < t_a.tab | cut -d' ' -f1)
HB=$(sha256sum < t_b.tab | cut -d' ' -f1)
HC=$(sha256sum < t_c.tab | cut -d' ' -f1)
printf 'sha256_seed1_run_a\t%s\nsha256_seed1_run_b\t%s\nsha256_seed7\t%s\n' "$HA" "$HB" "$HC"
test "$HA" = "$HB" || { echo "FAIL: two runs at seed 1 differ -- nothing here is reproducible"; exit 1; }
echo "identity_seed	two independent runs at seed 1 are byte-identical"

# Whether a DIFFERENT seed moves the result is REPORTED, not asserted: if it did not, that is a
# fact about this dataset, not a failure, and asserting it would be a check that can go flaky.
if [ "$HA" = "$HC" ]; then
  echo "seed_sensitivity	seed 7 gives byte-identical output to seed 1 on this fixture"
  echo "psms_with_a_changed_qvalue	0"
else
  # Compare whole (PSMId, peptide, q-value) records as SETS -- keying on PSMId alone would hit
  # the same non-uniqueness that broke identity 2.
  cut -f1,5,3 t_a.tab | tail -n +2 | sort > q_seed1.txt
  cut -f1,5,3 t_c.tab | tail -n +2 | sort > q_seed7.txt
  CHANGED=$(comm -23 q_seed1.txt q_seed7.txt | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  echo "seed_sensitivity	seed 7 gives a different ranking, so the seed is load-bearing"
  printf 'psms_with_a_changed_qvalue\t%s of %s\n' "$CHANGED" "$NT"
fi

{
  echo -e "observable\tvalue"
  printf 'pin_psm_rows\t%s\n' "$PROW"
  printf 'out_target_rows\t%s\n' "$NT"
  printf 'out_decoy_rows\t%s\n' "$ND"
  printf 'rows_in_the_wrong_class\t%s\n' "$MISPLACED"
  printf 'percolator_version\t%s\n' "${PV:-unknown}"
  printf 'sha256_seed1_run_a\t%s\n' "$HA"
  printf 'seed1_reproducible\tyes\n'
} > score.tsv
cat score.tsv | sed 's/^/  /'
cp score.tsv percolator-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "PERCOLATOR OK"
echo "DONE"
